definitions.explanation: Indicates something continuing without end. Used for genuine permanence, emotional emphasis, or hyperbolic expressions of a very long duration.

examples.japanese: {永遠|えいえん}に{忘|わす}れない。
この{瞬間|しゅんかん}が{永遠|えいえん}に{続|つづ}けばいいのに。
examples.english: I wish this moment would last forever.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}で{失|うしな}われた{命|いのち}は{永遠|えいえん}に{戻|もど}らない。
examples.english: Lives lost in war will never come back.

examples.japanese: この{会議|かいぎ}は{永遠|えいえん}に{終|お}わらないんじゃないかと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: I thought this meeting would never end.

notes:
Adverbial form of {永遠|えいえん} (eternity) + に. Used both literally (genuine permanence) and hyperbolically (feels like it will never end). Very common in emotional, poetic, and everyday contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {永遠|えいえん}に{続|つづ}く: to continue forever
- {永遠|えいえん}に{忘|わす}れない: to never forget
- {永遠|えいえん}に{失|うしな}われる: to be lost forever
- {永遠|えいえん}に{変|か}わらない: to never change

SIMILAR WORDS:
- いつまでも: forever; indefinitely — warmer and more colloquial, often used for wishes and hopes
- {永久|えいきゅう}に: permanently; perpetually — more formal and factual, emphasizes official or physical permanence
- ずっと: always; the whole time — emphasizes continuous duration from a point in time, less absolute than {永遠|えいえん}に
